We demonstrate that targeting the BCR::ABL1 breakpoint sequence efficiently degrades both wild-type and drug-resistant BCR::ABL1 mutants, which are the primary drivers of tyrosine kinase inhibitor resistance and relapse in chronic myeloid leukemia. Molecular profiling revealed that PspCas13b impairs BCR::ABL1 tyrosine phosphokinase activity and triggers extensive transcriptomic and proteomic remodeling, leading to erythroid differentiation and apoptosis in drug-resistant cells. Beyond BCR::ABL1, personalized design of PspCas13b effectively silences other undruggable oncogenic fusions. Collectively, this study establishes a molecular framework for precise targeting of undruggable or drug-resistant oncogenic transcripts.

title: lncRNA CHROMR promotes DLBCL viability and invasion in an m 6A-dependent manner.
abstract: Long noncoding RNA (lncRNA) CHROMR is closely associated with the development of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) and drug resistance to rituximab. However, the mechanism underlying the upregulation of the lncRNA CHROMR in DLBCL cells remains unknown. N 6-methyladenosine (m 6A) modifications are involved in the tumorigenesis and progression of numerous human cancers. This study reveals that m 6A complexes are enriched on the lncRNA CHROMR in DLBCL cells, as determined by methylated RNA immunoprecipitation-quantitative polymerase chain reaction (MeRIP-qPCR) assay and bioinformatics analysis. Our results demonstrate that methyltransferase-like 3 (METTL3) acts as the m 6A methylation writer for the lncRNA CHROMR at site 3 ("UGGAACUU"), while insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 1 (IGF2BP1) functions as the reader of this modification. Together, they enhance the stability of the lncRNA CHROMR. Furthermore, both METTL3 and IGF2BP1 play critical roles in regulating the viability and invasion of DLBCL cells. These findings highlight the indispensable role of m 6A modification in the lncRNA CHROMR, revealing METTL3 and IGF2BP1 as epigenetic mediators that regulate CHROMR expression.

title: Building Field-Ready Environmental RNA Panels.
abstract: Environmental RNA (eRNA) has been increasingly used to move beyond 'who is there' toward 'who is active' and 'what is happening' in ecosystems. Yet, most workflows have been optimised for laboratory sequencing, and decision-grade field use has remained sporadic. In this article, field-ready eRNA panels are defined as curated sets of transcripts paired with process controls and a transparent scoring rule, and a build-test pathway is described from marker discovery to deployment. Candidate markers are prioritised with field constraints in mind (abundance, specificity, persistence, and confounding seasonality), and RNA class choice (mRNA, rRNA, small, and other non-coding RNAs) is treated as a design lever for robustness. Pre-analytics are discussed as panel engineering, with emphasis placed on capture, rapid stabilisation, and inhibitor management to preserve multi-marker relationships. Field readout options are then compared, including isothermal amplification, CRISPR-assisted detection, portable qPCR, and portable nanopore sequencing for on-site verification and panel refresh. Finally, minimum controls and staged validation levels are proposed to support defensible ecological claims. Deliberate attention is directed toward shared terminology and testable standards so that discussion within and between ecology, diagnostics, and conservation practice is stimulated and priorities for future investigations are sharpened.

title: Genome-Wide Association and Genomic Prediction of Powdery Mildew and CYSDV Resistance in Melon.
abstract: Cucurbit powdery mildew (CPM) and Cucurbit yellow stunting disorder virus (CYSDV) are major constraints to sustainable melon (Cucumis melo L.) production worldwide. To elucidate the genetic basis of resistance and accelerate breeding, we integrated genome-wide association studies (GWASs), transcriptome validation, and genomic selection (GS) using a global panel of 341 melon accessions. Re-analysis of GWAS using BLINK and FarmCPU identified 18 and 19 marker-trait associations exceeding the exploratory threshold for CPM and CYSDV, respectively. Candidate gene analysis highlighted genes involved in lipid metabolism, membrane integrity, hormone signaling, transcriptional regulation, reactive oxygen species detoxification, and antiviral defense, including MLO-like protein, lipid transfer protein, hydroxyproline-rich glycoprotein, glutathione synthetase, RNA helicase, and elongation factor-like protein. Transcriptome analysis further validated several CPM-associated loci through infection-responsive expression patterns, strengthening their candidacy for disease resistance. Genomic prediction using Bayesian Ridge (BRR), gBLUP, Bayesian LASSO, Bayes A, and Bayes B, evaluated under 10-fold cross-validation, achieved consistently high prediction accuracies for CPM and moderate accuracies for CYSDV, reflecting differences in their underlying genetic architecture. Collectively, these findings identify putative associated resistance loci and demonstrate the utility of integrating GWAS, transcriptomics, and genomic selection to enhance marker-assisted and genomic-assisted breeding for durable resistance to fungal and viral diseases in melon.

title: OsVIPP1 Supports Rice Leaf Chloroplast Development and Is Associated with Seed Metabolic Changes and Yield-Related Traits.
abstract: Plastid membrane integrity is essential for plant growth, development, and metabolism, yet the functions of vesicle-inducing protein in plastids 1 (VIPP1) throughout the crop life cycle remain unclear. Here, we characterized OsVIPP1 in rice using CRISPR/Cas9 knockout, overexpression, and RNA-interference lines, together with ultrastructural, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and targeted biochemical analyses. osvipp1 knockout seedlings exhibited an albino-lethal phenotype, disorganized thylakoid membranes, disrupted intermembrane connections, and altered expression of chloroplast-encoded genes, supporting an essential role for OsVIPP1 in plastid membrane development. Both overexpression and RNA interference delayed seed germination, reduced plant height, and impaired yield-related traits. Integrated transcriptomic and untargeted metabolomic analyses associated altered OsVIPP1 expression with lipid, carbon, and phytohormone-related pathways. In overexpression seeds, abscisic acid content increased to 1.95 times the wild-type level, accompanied by the accumulation of several fatty acids and soluble sugars, whereas abscisic acid and most fatty acids decreased in RNA-interference seeds. These findings indicate that OsVIPP1 supports thylakoid spatial organization in leaves, whereas altered OsVIPP1 expression is associated with metabolic changes in mature seeds and yield-related phenotypes.

title: Folic Acid Oversupplementation Alters Global DNA Methylation and Circadian Clock Gene Expression in FaDu Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma Cells: An Exploratory Study.
abstract: Folic acid (FA), the synthetic form of folate (vitamin B9), is a vitamin involved in one-carbon metabolism, DNA synthesis, and DNA methylation. Because folate metabolism influences methyl donor availability, FA availability may affect circadian clock gene regulation through methylation-related or other metabolic mechanisms in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). This exploratory study aims to determine whether FA oversupplementation influences cell viability and alters global DNA methylation, as well as the expression and methylation status of circadian clock genes in HNSCC cells. FaDu HNSCC cells were treated with 20 or 80 μM FA and compared with a no-added-FA (NF) reference condition. Cell viability was assessed using a CCK-8 assay after 48 and 72 h. For methylation and gene expression analyses, cells were synchronized with forskolin and treated with FA (20 or 80 μM) for 7 days. Global DNA methylation was measured using a 5-methylcytosine colorimetric assay. Following the NF and 80 μM FA treatment, cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) island methylation in the BMAL1 and PER2 promoters, RNA expression, and protein levels were analyzed by bisulfite conversion followed by Sanger sequencing, qPCR, and ELISA. FA treatment significantly reduced cell viability at 48 h (20 μM, p < 0.05; 80 μM, p < 0.01) and 72 h (both concentrations p < 0.01). Global DNA methylation was modestly reduced, reaching statistical significance only in the 80 μM FA group (p < 0.05). No qualitative differences were observed in the promoter methylation of the analyzed CpG regions of BMAL1 and PER2 following 80 μM FA treatment. However, BMAL1 and PER2 mRNA expressions were significantly increased (p < 0.05), while protein levels showed non-significant upward trends following 80 μM FA treatment. These exploratory findings suggest that the observed transcriptional changes are unlikely to be explained by methylation changes within the analyzed promoter regions of BMAL1 and PER2. The mechanisms underlying these changes remain unclear and require further investigation.

title: Progesterone Modulates Protein Synthesis in Osteoarthritic Fibroblast-like Synoviocytes.
abstract: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is highly prevalent in women and is characterized by structural joint alterations and synovial inflammatory processes that contribute to pain and impaired mobility. In a previous study, we identified a positive correlation between progesterone levels and pain intensity in postmenopausal women. However, the role of progesterone in synovial inflammation remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study aimed to characterize sex-specific differences in synovial tissue between postmenopausal women and age-matched men and to investigate the association between progesterone levels and the identified molecular profile. Whole blood and synovial tissue were collected from women and men with knee OA to assess plasma progesterone concentrations and the proteomic profiles of synovial tissue and isolated primary fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLSs). The expression and localization of progesterone receptors were evaluated using RNAscope and immunofluorescence. FLS stimulated with physiological concentrations of progesterone were used for de novo protein synthesis assays. Quantitative proteomics of synovial tissue revealed enrichment of protein synthesis-related pathways in women compared to age-matched men, and isolated FLS from women with knee OA exhibited a pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic proteomic profile. Stratification by plasma progesterone levels identified two distinct patient groups, where lower progesterone levels were associated with pro-inflammatory signatures. The RNAscope analysis demonstrated increased transcriptional activity in synovial tissue from women with knee OA, localized to CD90+ sublining FLS. However, progesterone receptor expression at both the RNA and protein levels showed no sex-specific differences. Moreover, physiological concentrations of progesterone inhibited de novo protein synthesis in FLS isolated from men with knee OA. These findings underscore the hormonal context-dependent modulatory effects of progesterone on synovial inflammation and fibroblast activity. The study further highlights the importance of incorporating sex-specific hormonal profiles into OA patient stratification to support more precise and targeted therapeutic strategies.

title: Tunlametinib Suppresses Melanogenesis Induces Cell Cycle Arrest and Apoptosis in Giant Congenital Melanocytic Nevus Cells.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Giant congenital melanocytic nevus (GCMN) is a rare developmental disorder arising from abnormal proliferation and differentiation of neural crest-derived melanocytes. It poses substantial clinical challenges due to cosmetic disfigurement, malignant potential, and the limited efficacy of current treatments. This study aimed to investigate the therapeutic effects and underlying molecular mechanisms of tunlametinib (HL-085), a novel selective MEK1/2 inhibitor, in GCMN. Methods: Primary GCMN cells and human GCMN explants were isolated, cultured, and validated to establish in vitro cellular and explant models. Following tunlametinib treatment, global transcriptional changes were analyzed using bulk RNA sequencing. Melanogenesis was assessed via Fontana-Masson staining, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence. Cell viability, apoptosis, and cell cycle distribution were evaluated using the CCK-8 assay, flow cytometry, TUNEL staining, and Western blotting for apoptosis- and cell cycle-related proteins. Results: Tunlametinib treatment significantly suppressed melanogenesis in GCMN cells and explant tissues at the phenotypic, histological, and protein levels, and reduced cell viability in a concentration-dependent manner. Transcriptomic analysis revealed marked alterations in gene expression profiles following treatment, with prominent changes in apoptosis- and cell cycle-related genes. Subsequent cellular assays and tissue staining confirmed that tunlametinib significantly increased early apoptosis and induced G1/S cell cycle arrest. Conclusions: Collectively, our findings demonstrate that tunlametinib inhibits proliferation and melanin production in GCMN cells by modulating the RAS-ERK pathway, providing a theoretical basis for its use as a targeted therapeutic strategy for GCMN.

title: Multi-omics atlas of chronic exercise.
abstract: Exercise reduces all-cause mortality, yet its molecular effects across organs, sexes, and circadian phases remain incompletely understood. We subjected mice to 8 weeks of voluntary wheel running and collected 22 tissues and plasma during active and inactive phases for bulk RNA sequencing, metabolomics, proteomics, and single-nucleus RNA and methylation sequencing. Exercise induced canonical fiber-type switching and widespread, tissue-specific remodeling, with the largest transcriptomic changes in skeletal muscle. Except for the hypothalamus, kidney, and lung, most tissues changed more during the active phase. Females showed broader transcriptional responses, with distinct downregulation. Pairing single-nucleus methylomes with transcriptomes resolved the cell types driving exercise-induced epigenetic remodeling-changes undetectable by bulk studies. These included coordinated gene-body demethylation and transcription that tracked with fiber-type switching in specific myonuclei. Cell-type-resolved methylation, including partially methylated domains characterized in muscle, revealed a strong, sex-biased epigenetic response to training. Machine learning identified conserved exercise signatures across mammalian species.

title: Emerging frontiers for AI in single-cell genomics.
abstract: We are just over a decade into the single-cell revolution in biology, which has been coupled to the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) in single-cell genomics. Most early single-cell RNA embedding models and subsequent "foundation models"-representational models pretrained on large single-cell datasets-did not gain wide traction among experimental biologists. However, as massive single-cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) atlas efforts ramp up, there is a clear rationale for exploiting AI models to interpret new datasets in the context of vast existing data resources. Meanwhile, the advent of single-cell epigenetic/multiomic assays and Perturb-seq technologies presents new opportunities for AI modeling. Here, we review AI embedding and foundation models for scRNA-seq and single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin using sequencing (scATAC-seq), extensive machine-learning efforts to exploit single-cell multiome in regulatory genomics, and AI strategies to learn "virtual cell" models from Perturb-seq, ending with a description of current limitations of single-cell AI models and an outlook for future advances.

title: NEK2 promotes trastuzumab resistance in gastric cancer through WTAP/YTHDF1-dependent m6A regulation of FN1.
abstract: Trastuzumab resistance remains a major challenge in the clinical management of gastric cancer (GC), and effective strategies to overcome resistance are still limited. NEK2 has been implicated in GC progression and therapeutic resistance in several tumor types; however, its role in trastuzumab resistance in GC and the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Trastuzumab-resistant NCI-N87/TR cells were established from parental NCI-N87 cells by stepwise exposure to increasing concentrations of trastuzumab. NEK2 was markedly upregulated in trastuzumab-resistant GC cells. Silencing NEK2 attenuated trastuzumab resistance, as evidenced by decreased cell viability and DNA replication and increased apoptosis, whereas NEK2 overexpression enhanced resistance to trastuzumab. Mechanistically, NEK2 promoted FN1 expression and activated PI3K/AKT signaling, while exogenous FN1 partially rescued the inhibitory effect of NEK2 knockdown on trastuzumab resistance. RNA immunoprecipitation, MeRIP-qPCR, and dual-luciferase reporter assays analyses further showed that WTAP-dependent N6-methyladenosine (m6A) modification at nucleotide 5882 of FN1 mRNA, followed by YTHDF1 recognition, enhanced FN1 mRNA stability and protein expression. Moreover, overexpression of either WTAP or YTHDF1 restored FN1 expression, AKT phosphorylation, and trastuzumab resistance in NEK2-silenced cells. NEK2 promotes trastuzumab resistance in GC by enhancing WTAP/YTHDF1-dependent m6A regulation of FN1, thereby activating PI3K/AKT signaling. These findings suggest that NEK2 may represent a potential therapeutic target for overcoming trastuzumab resistance in GC.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Analysis Identifies Candidate Kinase-Mediated Thyroid-Associated Targets of Withaferin A.
abstract: Withaferin A (WA), a bioactive steroidal lactone derived from Withania somnifera, has been reported to exhibit diverse pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. Although previous studies suggest a potential link between WA and thyroid-related molecular pathways, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed a comprehensive computational approach to explore WA-responsive molecular changes potentially relevant to thyroid-associated processes. RNA-sequencing data from WA-treated MCF-10A human mammary epithelial cells (GSE158085) were analysed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Because thyroid-specific WA transcriptomic datasets are not currently available, the DEGs were intersected with curated hypothyroidism-associated genes to generate a cross-tissue, exploratory set of candidate genes. The genes that overlapped were used to construct protein-protein interaction networks, prioritize high-centrality candidate genes, and conduct enrichment analyses for transcription factors and kinases. Further analysis of selected upstream kinases was performed using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations with WA. A total of 1458 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, 10 of which overlapped with hypothyroidism-associated genes. Network analysis identified candidate interactions among the overlapping genes, while higher-confidence analysis retained four connected genes (PTPN22, STAT4, DUOX2, and DUOXA2). Transcription factor enrichment identified ERG, SUZ12, NANOG, TCF3, RUNX1, and TP63 as potential upstream regulators, while kinase enrichment identified candidate upstream kinases associated with the predicted regulatory network. Based on enrichment evidence, structural availability, and literature-supported biological relevance, MAPK14 (p38α), AKT1, and MAPK8 (JNK1) were selected for molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Structural analyses suggested potential interactions between WA and the selected kinases, with target-specific dynamic behaviour across the simulated systems. Collectively, the findings highlight WA-responsive genes and predicted gene-TF-kinase relationships that may be relevant to thyroid-associated molecular processes. However, these associations are hypothesis-generating and provide a basis for further investigation in thyroid-derived experimental models.

title: MCOF: A Multi-Channel Attention-Based Omics Fusion Framework for Cancer Subtyping and Candidate Biomarker Prioritization.
abstract: Multi-omics molecular subtyping is complicated by small cohorts, heterogeneous data layers, and sensitivity to data splitting and feature selection. We developed multi-channel attention-based omics fusion (MCOF), an end-to-end framework that combines omics-specific projection, one-dimensional convolution, and integrated gradients for candidate biomarker prioritization. MCOF was evaluated against six baselines using five repeated stratified holdouts across four multi-omics datasets. In the restricted four-class breast invasive carcinoma task, MCOF achieved the highest observed mean for all five metrics, including an accuracy of 0.900 ± 0.022 and a macro-averaged area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (macro-AUC) of 0.982 ± 0.003. In the restricted three-class stomach adenocarcinoma task, it achieved the highest observed macro-F1 (0.786 ± 0.035), macro-AUC (0.934 ± 0.020), and weighted-AUC (0.930 ± 0.016), whereas support vector machines had a slightly higher accuracy and weighted F1. It also achieved the highest or near-highest AUC on the two non-cancer datasets. Compared with MOGONET, MCOF used 30.6% fewer trainable parameters on both cancer tasks. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the contribution of multi-omics fusion varied by dataset and metric. Excluding the 28 prediction analysis of microarray 50 (PAM50) genes present in the retained BRCA RNA panel produced only a modest reduction in the macro-AUC, from 0.982 ± 0.003 to 0.978 ± 0.004. Implementation tests across 20 trained checkpoints detected no batch-order effect or cross-sample gradient, while the IG rankings were moderately stable across repeated holdouts and numerically consistent across class-weighting schemes and 25-100 integration steps. MCOF provides a practical framework for multi-omics classification and candidate prioritization.

title: Multi-Species Transcriptomics of the Mammalian Stomach Reveals Conserved Programs and Ruminant Chamber Specialization.
abstract: The mammalian stomach has conserved digestive functions but also shows major anatomical and physiological differences among species. However, broad comparative transcriptomic analyses across mammals and across ruminant stomach chambers remain limited. Here, we collected and integrated 111 bulk RNA-seq datasets from 11 mammalian species (humans, mice, monkeys, dogs, horses, donkeys, pigs, cattle, deer, goats, and sheep) and analyzed 12,048 shared one-to-one orthologous genes. We identified 56 conserved genes mainly involved in translation, ribosome biogenesis, protein homeostasis, and mitochondrial function. Pairwise comparisons revealed extensive transcriptional differences, with 2070-7110 differentially expressed genes across species pairs, together with distinct species-associated transcription-factor activity patterns. We also identified 25 ruminant-enriched genes associated with epithelial differentiation, ion transport, mucosal defense, and metabolism. Analysis of 69 samples from the rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum of sheep, goats, cattle, and deer showed clear chamber-associated transcriptomic differences. The abomasum had a distinct expression program, with 235 enriched genes related to hormone regulation, secretion, transport, and digestion. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis further identified different gene programs in the forestomach and abomasum. Together, these findings reveal conserved, species-associated, and chamber-associated transcriptional features of the mammalian stomach and provide a useful framework for understanding its molecular diversity.

title: HLA-Engineered iPSC-Derived Mesenchymal Stromal Cells for the Treatment of Osteoarthritis in Mice.
abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is one of the most prevalent degenerative joint diseases, and there is no approved pharmacological therapy that can reliably reverse cartilage degeneration or restore cartilage structure. Allogeneic mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) have shown therapeutic potential for OA, but inflammatory conditions can enhance HLA expression and increase allogeneic immune recognition risk. Here, we generated B2M and CIITA double-knockout induced pluripotent stem cells (dKO-iPSCs) using CRISPR/Cas9 and subsequently differentiated them into dKO-iMSCs. B2M/CIITA double-knockout did not affect iPSC pluripotency, karyotype, or teratoma formation. dKO-iMSCs retained characteristic MSC phenotypes, exhibited greater proliferative capacity than tissue-derived MSCs, and could be expanded to passage 18. Notably, HLA-ABC and HLA-DR expression remained undetectable in dKO-iMSCs even after IFN-γ stimulation. In co-culture assays with PHA-L-stimulated allogeneic PBMCs, dKO-iMSCs suppressed PBMC and T-cell proliferation as effectively as wild-type iMSCs, indicating preservation of their immunomodulatory activity. Intra-articular administration of dKO-iMSCs significantly reduced cartilage degeneration in the destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) mouse model of OA. The treatment showed greater therapeutic efficacy than wild-type iMSCs and tissue-derived MSCs and did not cause evident systemic organ toxicity. Single-cell RNA sequencing of BM-MSCs and dKO-iMSCs after in vitro IFN-γ stimulation revealed enhanced extracellular matrix-associated cell-cell communication and markedly reduced IL1B expression in dKO-iMSCs, indicating a less pro-inflammatory and more matrix-supportive cellular state under inflammatory conditions. Collectively, B2M/CIITA double-knockout enables sustained reduction in HLA expression while preserving the MSC phenotype and immunomodulatory activity, and enhances the therapeutic efficacy of iMSCs in the mouse OA model, providing a potential strategy for developing iPSC-derived MSCs with reduced HLA expression for allogeneic cell therapy.

title: Melatonin Regulates Sheep Granulosa Cell Proliferation and Apoptosis Through a Novel Micropeptide, IGF1Raa.
abstract: Melatonin is a hormone primarily secreted by the pineal gland, best known for regulating circadian rhythms. It also plays a critical role in ovarian physiology by modulating granulosa cell (GC) function during follicular development, although the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Recent advances in ribosome sequencing (Ribo-seq) have revealed that many small open reading frames (sORFs), previously overlooked in conventional annotations, actually encode functional micropeptides. However, whether melatonin exerts its ovarian effects through such micropeptides has remained unexplored. In the present study, we identified a previously unannotated sORF within the 5'untranslated region (UTR) of sheep IGF1R mRNA and demonstrated that this sORF encodes a 32-amino-acid micropeptide, which we named IGF1Raa. Knockdown and overexpression of IGF1Raa in sheep GCs, assessed by CCK-8, Edu, flow cytometry, and ELISA, revealed that IGF1Raa negatively regulates GC proliferation and E2 secretion and promotes apoptosis. Co-ip assays and RNA-seq show that IGF1Raa physically associates with PPP2R2B, a regulatory subunit of protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), and modulates PP2A protein expression. Consequently, IGF1Raa regulates the phosphorylation of AMPK (Thr172) and its downstream effector Raptor (Ser792), thereby controlling the AMPK/mTOR signaling cascade. Importantly, melatonin suppresses IGF1Raa expression, and overexpression of IGF1Raa partially abrogates melatonin's stimulatory effects on GC proliferation and steroidogenesis. Collectively, our findings identify IGF1Raa as a melatonin-responsive micropeptide that governs GC function through the PP2A/AMPK/mTOR axis, providing new insights into the regulatory network of ovarian physiology and offering potential therapeutic targets for reproductive disorders.

title: A phase 2a study with SPL84: A novel RNA-targeted approach to restore CFTR function in people with CF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation.
abstract: The 3849+10 kb C→T mutation in the Cystic Fibrosis Transmembrane Conductance Regulator (CFTR) gene leads to aberrant splicing and the inclusion of a cryptic exon harboring a premature stop codon, resulting in the production of non-functional CFTR protein. SPL84 is an inhaled antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) designed to correct CFTR splicing and restore functional CFTR expression in people with CF (pwCF) carrying this mutation. This Phase 2a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, multiple ascending dose study evaluated safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and exploratory efficacy of inhaled SPL84 in pwCF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation. Participants received once-weekly inhalations of SPL84 (25 or 50 mg) or placebo for 9 weeks. Exploratory efficacy measures included changes in ppFEV1, ppFEF25-75, and CFQ-R respiratory symptom score. Seventeen participants were included in the analysis, with fifteen completing all treatments. SPL84 was well tolerated with no drug-related serious adverse events. Most adverse events were mild or moderate and consistent with the underlying CF disease. Improvements in lung function, defined as change from baseline in ppFEV1≥5, were observed in up to 70% of the treated participants per cohort, accompanied by improvement of additional efficacy outcomes. Inhaled SPL84 demonstrated a favorable safety profile together with encouraging signals of clinical benefit in pwCF carrying the 3849+10 kb C→T mutation. These findings represent, to our knowledge, the first evidence of potential clinical benefit from a nucleic acid-based therapy targeting RNA in a pulmonary disease, supporting further evaluation of SPL84 as a mutation-specific, RNA-targeted treatment.

title: NUPR1-positive tumor-associated macrophages facilitate the progression of hepatocellular carcinoma via ferroptosis resistance.
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are major contributors to the immunosuppressive microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Nuclear protein 1 (NUPR1) is a stress-responsive regulator implicated in tumor progression; however, whether it functionally controls ferroptosis-associated stress adaptation in TAMs and thereby sustains their immunosuppressive phenotype remains unclear. Single-cell RNA sequencing and multiplex immunohistochemistry identified and validated NUPR1-expressing TAMs in human HCC. Pharmacological and genetic approaches assessed macrophage polarization, ferroptosis-associated changes, and tumor-supportive activity. Readouts included lipid peroxidation, Fe2+ accumulation, GPX4 expression and activity, redox homeostasis, and mitochondrial membrane potential. GPX4 rescue and pharmacological ferroptosis modulation evaluated the functional involvement of GPX4-associated ferroptosis resistance. Primary bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) and an immunocompetent orthotopic HCC model provided additional validation. NUPR1 was enriched in CD163+ TAMs within HCC tissues. In THP-1-derived macrophages, NUPR1 inhibition enhanced ferroptosis-associated changes and attenuated M2-like polarization and tumor-supportive functions, whereas NUPR1 overexpression produced the opposite effects. GPX4 overexpression partially rescued the ferroptosis-associated and macrophage phenotypic changes induced by NUPR1 silencing, whereas RSL3 attenuated the effects of NUPR1 overexpression. Primary BMDMs supported the macrophage phenotypic findings. In the orthotopic model, NUPR1 inhibition suppressed tumor growth and was accompanied by altered macrophage-associated markers and enhanced ferroptosis-associated changes. NUPR1 promotes HCC progression, at least in part, by modulating GPX4-associated ferroptosis-related stress and sustaining the M2-like immunosuppressive phenotype of TAMs.

title: ELF1 exacerbates intervertebral disc degeneration by promoting ACSL4-dependent ferro-aging of nucleus pulposus cells through the IFITM3-PTPRO axis.
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is a major cause of low back pain and is characterized by nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) senescence and extracellular matrix degradation. Ferro-aging, a chronic iron-dependent lipid peroxidation-associated senescence program, has recently been proposed as a potential mechanism linking metabolic dysregulation with tissue aging. However, whether ferro-aging contributes to IVDD and how it is regulated remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of ferro-aging in IVDD and identify its upstream regulatory network. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, human nucleus pulposus tissue validation, puncture-induced and age-related IVDD animal models, and multiple NPC senescence models were used to investigate IFITM3-associated ferro-aging. Loss- and gain-of-function approaches, RNA sequencing, co-immunoprecipitation, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays were performed to investigate the regulatory network involving ELF1, IFITM3, PTPRO, and ACSL4. IFITM3 showed increased expression in degenerated NPCs and was associated with ferroptosis-related pathways, inflammatory responses, and extracellular matrix remodeling. IFITM3 promoted NPC ferro-aging by enhancing iron accumulation, ACSL4 expression, lipid peroxidation, oxidative stress, and cellular senescence. Mechanistically, PTPRO was identified as an IFITM3-associated regulatory node that contributes to ACSL4 protein stabilization and lipid peroxidation, while ELF1 transcriptionally activates IFITM3. Genetic inhibition of Ifitm3, Ptpro, or Elf1 alleviated ferro-aging phenotypes and attenuated IVDD progression. This study identifies ferro-aging as a previously unrecognized mechanism contributing to IVDD and identifies a regulatory network involving ELF1, IFITM3, PTPRO, and ACSL4 as a potential therapeutic framework for delaying disc degeneration.

title: Development and Characterization of a Rat Model of Post-traumatic Ankle Osteoarthritis.
abstract: The molecular mechanisms contributing to posttraumatic ankle osteoarthritis (PTAOA) remain unclear. Here, we developed a rat model of PTAOA induced by joint instability and evaluated both pain and pathological changes. We paid special attention to the synovial tissue, which acts as a critical, pain-generating structure in OA. We induced ankle instability by resection of the anterior talofibular ligament (ATFL) and calcaneofibular ligament (CFL) (RAC group). Safranin-O and hematoxylin & eosin staining were conducted to evaluate histological changes. Pain-related behavior was also assessed. Bulk RNA sequencing for dorsal root ganglia (DRG) and single-cell RNA sequencing for synovial tissues were performed to examine molecular changes in PTAOA. Cartilage loss (Mean Difference (MD)=0.52, 95%CI: -0.019 to 1.060) and synovitis (MD=2.24, 95% CI: 1.473 to 3.009) were observed in the ankle joints of RAC rats (n=8), compared to the Sham control (n=8). Pain also developed in PTAOA rats. RNA sequencing revealed that the TGF-β-MAPK/PI3K-Akt-CTGF signaling axis and the THBS2-FN1 axis were activated in PTAOA synovial tissue. In particular, suppressing THBS2 expression decreased fibrosis marker expression in human fibroblast culture. Lastly, systemic administration of meloxicam reduced pain in PTAOA rats compared with the placebo group (MD=50.4, 95% CI: 4.8 to 96.1) (n=8 per group). This study sheds light on the pathological changes in synovial tissue and identifies key pathways involved in PTAOA. The findings suggest novel therapeutic targets for managing PTAOA. Additionally, the PTAOA model developed in this research can be used as a preclinical model to test potential treatments.

title: Beyond the Transcriptome: The m6A Epitranscriptome in Bovine Mastitis.
abstract: Bovine mastitis is a heterogeneous inflammatory disease that compromises milk production, animal welfare and dairy sustainability. Despite extensive transcriptomic and epigenomic research, a PubMed search completed in September 2026 identified only 12 primary studies addressing epitranscriptomic regulation in bovine mastitis, representing approximately 0.1% of indexed publications. This review critically evaluates N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most extensively studied RNA modification in bovine mastitis, its regulatory machinery and effects on mammary immunity, while identifying m5C and A-to-I editing as priorities for mechanistic investigation. Current evidence identifies transcript-specific RNA stability as the best-supported mechanism and provides a foundation for investigating m6A-dependent translation. Functional studies of ALKBH5-LOC4191, YTHDF2-IER3, YTHDF2-associated CCL20 and CCL5 regulation, m6A-regulated LncRNA7825 and FTO-FN1 demonstrate that m6A reshapes inflammatory signalling, mitochondrial stress, epithelial-barrier integrity, cell survival and bacterial control. Synthesizing these findings, we propose a context-dependent RNA-fate checkpoint model in which biological effects depend on the modified transcript, effector protein, pathogen, cellular context and infection phase. The FTO-FN1 axis shows that bacterial control and tissue protection can diverge, establishing them as complementary outcomes. Future studies should test whether m6A provides an early post-transcriptional response layer and whether pathogens manipulate it, using time-resolved multi-omics, nucleotide-specific perturbation, primary cells, mammary organoids and longitudinal cattle samples. Parallel profiling of non-m6A modifications should define interacting regulatory layers. These approaches should establish causal modification sites, resolve pathogen-specific regulation, connect molecular mechanisms with disease trajectories, and support validated milk-based biomarkers, mammary-targeted interventions and prioritization of stable genetic variants for breeding mastitis-resistant cattle.

title: Exogenous Melatonin Alleviates High- and Low-Temperature Stress in Cucumber Seedlings and Regulates Hormone Signaling-Related Transcriptional Responses.
abstract: Temperature stress is a major environmental factor that limits the growth of cucumber (Cucumis sativus L.). Melatonin has been implicated in plant responses to abiotic stress; however, its transcriptional effects on cucumber under high- and low-temperature conditions remain poorly understood. In this study, cucumber seedlings were exposed to 25 °C, 40 °C, or 4 °C, with or without exogenous melatonin treatment at 75 μmol·L-1, and their transcriptional responses were investigated using RNA sequencing (RNA-seq). Both high- and low-temperature treatments caused varying degrees of seedling wilting, whereas this phenotype was partially alleviated by melatonin application. Transcriptome analysis identified 7488 and 3400 differentially expressed genes in response to high and low temperatures, respectively, indicating both shared and temperature-specific transcriptional responses. Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analysis showed that pathways related to plant hormone signal transduction, phenylpropanoid biosynthesis, and protein processing in the endoplasmic reticulum were significantly enriched in multiple comparisons. Further analysis revealed that melatonin treatment altered the expression patterns of several hormone signaling-related genes and transcription factors, including members of the ERF, MYB, WRKY, and bHLH families. Notably, hormone signaling components exhibited distinct transcriptional responses under high- and low-temperature conditions. The expression trends of selected genes determined by quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were generally consistent with the RNA-seq results. Collectively, exogenous melatonin application was associated with reduced wilting symptoms and coordinated transcriptional changes in hormone signaling pathways under temperature stress. These findings provide a basis for further elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying melatonin-mediated temperature adaptation in cucumber seedlings.

title: Integrated Physiological, Transcriptomic, and Proteomic Analyses Reveal Alkali Stress Response and Tolerance Mechanisms of Rhododendron obtusum 'Fenzhuanglou' Seedlings.
abstract: Soil alkalization limits the cultivation of Rhododendron, an acidophilic ornamental genus, yet the alkali tolerance threshold of R. obtusum 'Fenzhuanglou' remains undefined. Seedlings were exposed for 40 d to mixed alkali (NaHCO3:Na2CO3 = 9:1; 0, 50, 60, and 70 mmol·L-1), combining physiological assays with RNA-seq and DIA proteomics of control and 60 mmol·L-1 leaves. The 50 mmol·L-1 treatment caused no visible injury, 60 mmol·L-1 defined the visible-injury threshold, and 70 mmol·L-1 caused severe, progressive damage. Chlorophyll b fell to about 20% of the control by 40 d under 60-70 mmol·L-1; antioxidant enzymes peaked at 20 d and then collapsed, while malondialdehyde accumulated dose-dependently, indicating late-stage failure of reactive oxygen species scavenging. Transcriptomics identified 7214 differentially expressed genes enriched in MAPK signaling, hormone signal transduction, and circadian rhythm; proteomics quantified 7452 proteins, including 1093 differentially expressed proteins enriched in flavonoid biosynthesis and α-linolenic acid metabolism. The low mRNA-protein correlation (ρ = 0.14-0.20) is consistent with transcript-protein decoupling potentially involving post-transcriptional regulation, protein stability, and turnover. These results define 60 mmol·L-1 as the tolerance limit of this cultivar and, to our knowledge, provide the first integrated multi-omics framework for alkali adaptation in Rhododendron.

title: Transcriptomic Profiling of Adherent Cells Isolated from Wedged Pulmonary Arterial Blood of Patients with Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Reveals a Predominantly Myeloid Rather than Endothelial Phenotype.
abstract: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is characterized by progressive vascular remodeling and immune dysregulation. Myeloid angiogenic cells (MACs) are blood-derived mononuclear cells that acquire endothelial-like features at sites of vascular injury, but their transcriptomic phenotype in the pulmonary vascular compartment is poorly characterized. We isolated adherent cells from blood aspirated from the wedged pulmonary artery of four patients with severe PAH during right heart catheterization. The cells were vWF-positive and ACTA2-negative by immunocytochemistry and co-expressed canonical endothelial (CDH5, PECAM1, ERG, FLT1) and myeloid (PTPRC/CD45, CD14, SPI1, IRF8) transcripts, consistent with MAC-like adherent cultures rather than a conventional endothelial population. Bulk RNA sequencing of these cultures was compared with human pulmonary artery endothelial cells (HPAECs) and HUVECs used as endothelial reference cultures. Relative to both references, PAH MACs showed higher transcript levels of cytokines (IL1A, TNF, IL15, IL10) and matrix metalloproteinases (MMP8/9/12); relative to HPAECs, they showed lower levels of Notch-associated genes (DLL4, HEYL). Protein-protein interaction analysis identified modules centered on complement components, myeloid immune receptors and CC chemokines. Because MACs from non-PAH subjects were not available, these differences describe the phenotype of PAH-derived MACs relative to endothelial reference cells rather than a PAH-specific effect. Adherent cultures obtained from wedged pulmonary arterial blood are therefore dominated by a mononuclear phagocyte transcriptional program, which has direct implications for the design of patient-derived pulmonary vascular cell models.

title: Integrated Multi-Omics Analysis Reveals Molecular Signatures Associated with Growth Divergence in Mandarin Fish (Siniperca chuatsi).
abstract: Within-cohort growth heterogeneity constrains aquaculture productivity, and its molecular correlates in carnivorous teleosts are poorly described. We compared the three heaviest and the three lightest individuals (n = 3 biological replicates per group, one fish per replicate) from a single cohort of mandarin fish (Siniperca chuatsi) at 90 days post-hatch, which differed 3.09-fold in body mass (p = 7.1 × 10-5), by combining muscle RNA sequencing with label-free quantitative proteomics of muscle and liver. Muscle transcriptomics identified 827 differentially expressed genes. The proteasome (ko03050) was the only KEGG pathway reaching significance, with all 14 contributing subunits being more abundant in slow-growing fish, and GO enrichment recovered proteasome, peptidase and endopeptidase complexes alongside serine-type peptidase activities in the same direction. Proteomics identified 37 differentially abundant proteins in muscle and 24 in liver at a nominal threshold. Protein-level gene set enrichment analysis showed negative enrichment of oxidative phosphorylation (NES = -1.96, adjusted p = 0.001) and of mitochondrial proteins (NES = -1.77, adjusted p = 0.005) in fast-growing muscle. Haemoglobin subunits were more abundant in fast-growing muscle and liver at the protein level, while muscle haemoglobin transcripts showed paralog-specific differences. The cross-sectional extreme-phenotype design identifies molecular signatures associated with the observed growth phenotype without establishing causality. The dataset provides candidate genes and proteins for functional study in S. chuatsi.

title: Chronic Cortisol Exposure Reshapes Chromatin Accessibility and Gene Expression: Implications for Growth and Welfare in Rainbow Trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss).
abstract: Cortisol, the principal glucocorticoid in teleosts, coordinates the physiological response to stress by regulating metabolism, protein turnover, and growth. Although the molecular effects of acute cortisol exposure have been extensively characterized, the epigenomic mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle remodeling during prolonged cortisol elevation remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how chronic cortisol reshapes chromatin accessibility and gene expression in rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss) skeletal muscle using an integrative ATAC-seq and RNA-seq approach. Fish received a single intraperitoneal injection of cortisol (50 μg g-1 body weight) formulated in coconut oil for sustained hormone release and were sampled after 14 days. Cortisol treatment significantly increased plasma cortisol levels, reduced specific growth rate, and increased skeletal muscle protein carbonylation, indicating impaired growth and oxidative protein damage. ATAC-seq revealed extensive chromatin remodeling, including 126,780 cortisol-specific accessible regions and 3393 genes associated with increased accessibility. These genes were enriched in pathways related to FoxO signaling, autophagy, and apoptosis, whereas regions with reduced accessibility were associated with TGF-β signaling, extracellular matrix interactions, and muscle structural maintenance. RNA-seq identified 2170 differentially expressed genes (844 upregulated and 1326 downregulated), revealing a parallel transcriptional shift toward protein turnover, autophagy, and metabolic adaptation, together with repression of extracellular matrix organization, focal adhesion, integrin signaling, and cytoskeletal organization. Integrative analysis identified 113 genes with coordinated increases and 46 genes with coordinated decreases in chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance, highlighting ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis, mitophagy, FoxO signaling, and metabolic pathways as core components of the chronic cortisol response. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that sustained cortisol elevation drives coordinated epigenomic and transcriptomic remodeling of skeletal muscle, promoting a catabolic phenotype characterized by enhanced protein turnover, oxidative protein damage, and impaired structural maintenance, ultimately contributing to reduced growth and potentially compromising fish welfare under aquaculture conditions.

title: Molecular Mechanisms Underlying α-Linolenic Acid-Enhanced Reproductive Performance in Male Blue Foxes.
abstract: α-Linolenic acid (ALA), an essential n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid, exerts critical effects on animal reproductive function. However, the molecular mechanisms by which dietary ALA regulates reproductive performance in male blue foxes remain largely unclear. In the present study, 16 male blue foxes of similar age and condition were assigned to four dietary groups (n = 4 per group) receiving a basal diet supplemented with 0, 0.5, 1.25, or 2 g/kg of ALA. q-PCR validation further confirmed that medium-dose ALA supplementation significantly upregulated mRNA levels of steroid synthesis-related genes (StAR, LHCGR, INSL3) and antioxidant gene GPX3, while inhibiting the calcium-signaling gene GRIN1. Untargeted liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) metabolomics of seminal plasma and RNA-seq transcriptomics of testicular tissue were combined to explore the underlying molecular pathways of ALA in terms of its modulating male blue fox reproduction. A total of eight significantly altered seminal plasma metabolites were screened out through metabolomics: mainly arachidonic acid, anandamide, oxaloacetic acid, guanine, lactic acid, dihydrodaidzein, stearic acid, and valylisoleucine. Transcriptomic analysis identified seven differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including FRAS1, COL1A1, CDH17, CLDN4, CTH, KYAT1, and GRIN1, enriched in three core KEGG pathways: ECM-receptor interaction, cell-adhesion molecules and selenocompound metabolism. Spearman correlation analysis revealed extensive significant correlations between seminal-plasma differential metabolites and testicular genes, indicating complicated metabolite-gene crosstalk. Collectively, appropriate dietary ALA remodels the seminal-plasma metabolic microenvironment, stabilizes testicular tissue structure, enhances gonadal antioxidant capacity and facilitates testicular steroidogenesis, thereby improving the reproductive potential of male blue foxes. This study elucidates the nutritional regulatory mechanism of ALA in breeding male blue foxes and provides theoretical references for the application of ALA as a functional feed additive in the production of canines.

title: Cross-Dataset Genomic Proximity and Functional Association of FOXA1 and TET2 at Hypomethylated Regulatory Regions in Colorectal Cancer.
abstract: Aberrant DNA methylation plays a critical role in the development and progression of colorectal cancer (CRC). However, how pioneer transcription factors are associated with DNA demethylases at cis-regulatory elements and influence tumor-associated transcriptional programs remains poorly understood. This study investigated the functional relationship between FOXA1 and TET2, an enzyme that converts 5-methylcytosine (5mC) to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), and its association with epigenetic features and malignant phenotypes in CRC. Public DNA methylation, ChIP-seq, and transcriptomic datasets were integrated with genome-wide genomic-proximity analyses. The association between FOXA1 and TET2 was evaluated by co-immunoprecipitation. FOXA1 and TET2 were individually or simultaneously depleted in HCT116 and SW480 cells, followed by proliferation and invasion assays. In addition, RNA-seq profiles were generated from control, FOXA1-KD, TET2-KD, and Double-KD HCT116 cells to characterize the resulting transcriptional changes. CRC-associated hypomethylated regions showed preferential enrichment of FOXA1- and TET2-associated ChIP-seq signals. At a 500 bp summit-to-summit threshold, FOXA1-TET2 genomic proximity was 30.7-fold higher than expected under chromosome-wise circular permutation (empirical p = 0.000999). FOXA1/TET2-associated loci also showed lower methylation than FOXA1-only loci in TCGA-COAD tumors (median within-patient Δβ = -0.051; paired Wilcoxon p = 5.86 × 10-50), and FOXA1 and TET2 expression was positively correlated in TCGA-COAD tumors (Spearman's ρ = 0.40 and p = 8.5 × 10-10). Co-immunoprecipitation supported the presence of FOXA1 and TET2 within the same protein complex but did not establish direct physical binding. FOXA1 depletion reduced cell-growth-associated and invasion-associated readouts in both CRC cell lines, whereas TET2 depletion increased growth-associated readouts and showed cell-line-dependent effects on invasion. Combined FOXA1/TET2 depletion produced an intermediate growth phenotype under the conditions examined. RNA-seq revealed broadly concordant transcriptome-wide changes among the knockdown conditions, with pairwise log2 fold-change correlations ranging from r = 0.835 to 0.920, together with shared and comparison-specific transcriptional responses.

title: Differential Enteric Glial and Mast Cell Characteristics Distinguish Microscopic Colitis Subtypes Relative to Healthy and Disease Controls, with Treatment-Associated Reductions in Glial Reactivity and Mast Cell Degranulation in Collagenous Colitis.
abstract: Microscopic colitis (MC) is an inflammatory bowel disease characterized by chronic watery diarrhea. Although barrier dysfunction and immune activation are implicated, underlying mechanisms remain unclear. The aim of this study was to characterize enteric glial cells (EGC) and mast cell distribution across MC subtypes, assess treatment effects, and explore EGC-related gene expression and barrier markers. Colonic biopsies from patients with active collagenous colitis (aCC), budesonide-refractory CC (rCC), and active lymphocytic colitis (LC) were compared to irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), ulcerative colitis (UC), and healthy controls (HC). A subset of CC patients was studied during active disease (aCC) and in clinical remission due to budesonide treatment (tCC). Immunofluorescence quantified EGC positive for glial fibrillary acidic protein (EGCGFAP+) and S100 calcium-binding protein B (EGCS100β+), mast cell tryptase, and tight junction proteins. RNA-sequencing assessed EGC-related gene expression. Results showed that EGCGFAP+ were highest in rCC and decreased following budesonide treatment in aCC, whereas EGCS100β+ were highest in aCC, remained unchanged following treatment, resembled IBS, and were reduced compared with UC. Mast cell numbers were higher in aCC than in HC and rCC but remained unchanged following treatment, while mast cell degranulation decreased after treatment. Tight junction proteins were unchanged. RNA-sequencing indicated differential regulation of EGC-related genes. In conclusion, MC shows subtype-specific alterations involving EGC and mast cells, suggesting distinct glial states and differential treatment responsiveness. Our findings support the presence of distinct neuroimmune alterations in CC and LC and highlight EGC as potential contributors to MC pathophysiology.

title: BIRC3 facilitates osteogenic differentiation of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells via NGFR/β-catenin signalling axis.
abstract: Osteoporosis primarily results from age-related declines in bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) differentiation into osteoblasts; however, the regulatory mechanisms remain unclear. Integrated analysis of Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) data identified a key osteogenic regulator. Western blot, reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), RNA-seq, immunohistochemistry (IHC), alkaline phosphatase (ALP), and alizarin red S (ARS) staining were employed to elucidate the functional and mechanistic aspects of modulating osteogenic differentiation. A C57 mouse tibial drill-hole model was used to evaluate therapeutic potential. RNA-seq identified baculoviral inhibitor of apoptosis (IAP) repeat-containing protein 3 (BIRC3) as a potential regulator of BMSC osteogenesis, showing significant upregulation during BMSC osteogenic differentiation and upon monocyte stimulation. BIRC3 positively correlated with ALP and ARS staining intensity and significantly enhanced the expression of (runt-related transcription factor 2) RUNX2 and ALP proteins. RNA-seq, RT-qPCR, and western blot data indicated that BIRC3 positively regulates the expression of nerve growth factor receptor (NGFR). NGFR also promoted the osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs. Further experiments demonstrated that BIRC3 regulates BMSC osteogenesis through NGFR. Through XAV939 treatment, we demonstrated that both BIRC3 and NGFR promoted BMSC osteogenesis by enhancing β-catenin expression and nuclear translocation, thereby defining the functional role of the BIRC3/NGFR/β-catenin axis in BMSCs. In C57 mouse tibial bone defect models, BIRC3 overexpression group exhibited significantly enhanced callus formation and ossification compared to the control group. BIRC3 regulates BMSC osteogenic differentiation via NGFR/β-catenin signalling in vitro and promotes bone healing in vivo, suggesting therapeutic potential for osteoporosis and bone defects.

title: The comprehensive transcriptomic profiling of RNA classes for biomonitoring and mechanistic studies.
abstract: The effects of various chemical compounds exposure on genetic material, including the risks of disease, are frequently evaluated by analyses of biomarkers. Among them, RNA markers play an important role in understanding the changes of transcriptomic processes. In this research we tested a new methodological approach of RNA libraries preparation in combination with sequencing to analyze the full transcriptome, including fragmented RNAs. Samples collected from firefighters at three time points were analyzed. A wide range of RNA types [non-coding RNAs (rRNA, tRNA, miRNA, snRNA, snoRNA, lncRNA, piRNA) and protein coding mRNAs] were detected simultaneously which allowed us to track the dynamics of their expression. The application of this comprehensive RNA profiling in a future biomonitoring study is promising: (i) for identification of the novel biomarkers of specific exposures; and (ii) to study the complex mechanisms of transcription including protective modifications, and/or harmful deregulations increasing the risk of diseases, e.g. cancer.

title: Inferring gene regulatory networks from single-cell transcriptomics jointly through graph neural networks and Transformer.
abstract: Inferring gene regulatory networks (GRNs) is crucial for understanding the complex regulatory relationships that govern gene expression in cells. Recently, several computational methods have been proposed for reconstructing GRNs from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, most of these methods primarily focus on pairwise regulatory relationships between genes, failing to leverage the global regulatory structure of GRNs, which is crucial for exploring the complex regulatory interactions between transcription factors (TFs) and their target genes. To address these limitations, we propose GTGRNS, a supervised learning framework that integrates a graph neural network with a Transformer encoder for GRN inference from scRNA-seq data. Specifically, we utilize the GraphSAGE model to integrate regulatory network topological information with gene expression features, facilitating the learning of gene representations. By leveraging the Transformer model, we further extract complex dependencies of gene pairs, which are crucial for determining regulatory levels. The comparative experiments on several benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed GTGRNS in the task of GRN inference.

title: Proteomic Profiling of Endometriosis and Ovarian Endometrioid Carcinoma: A Preliminary Exploratory Study.
abstract: IntroductionEndometriosis (EMs) is considered the precursor lesions of ovarian endometrioid carcinoma (OEC). This study aimed to identify differentially expressed proteins between OEC and EMs, and to explore the associated biological functional alterations.Materials and MethodsThis study conducted qualitative and quantitative label-free proteomic analysis on postoperative formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) specimens from 20 patients with EMs and 54 patients with OEC coexisting with EMs. A discovery set was established based on cluster random sampling, and differentially expressed proteins between the two groups were progressively screened. The identified candidates were then validated in an independent test cohort, followed by external validation using public transcriptomic datasets (GSE295399, GSE105764, GSE281569) from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database.ResultsThe OEC group exhibited a distinct protein expression profile compared to the EMs group. Seven differentially expressed hub proteins (SNRPD1, HNRNPC, NOP58, SRSF6, DHX9, SF3B3, and DHX15) were identified from the discovery cohort, all of which showed significantly altered expression in the test cohort (p < 0.0001). External transcriptomic validation confirmed consistent upregulation for five of the seven hub proteins in OEC compared to EMs (NOP58, SRSF6, DHX9, SF3B3, and DHX15; p < 0.001).ConclusionThis study identified and validated seven differentially expressed proteins associated with RNA splicing in OEC relative to EMs. These findings offer candidate molecules associated with the transition from benign endometriosis to ovarian endometrioid carcinoma; however, further functional studies are required to determine whether they may actively drive malignant transformation.

title: Downregulation of GJA1-Derived circ_753 and circ_755 Differentially Modulates miR-182-5p Expression and Breast Cancer-Associated Phenotypes.
abstract: CircRNAs are key regulators of gene expression. The functional roles of exonic versus exon-intron circRNAs in early breast cancer remain unclear. Connexin-43 (GJA1) generates exonic circRNA (ecircRNA) hsa_circ_0077755 (circ_755) and exon-intron circRNA (EIcircRNA), hsa_circ_0077753 (circ_753), both linked to increased breast cancer risk. We examined their structural, molecular, and phenotypic roles in transient and stable knockdown S1 breast epithelial cells, using RT-qPCR, dual-luciferase, lumen formation and invasion assays, and extracellular vesicle (EV) analysis. Knockdown of cytoplasm-enriched circ_755 reduced Connexin-43 transcript and protein, whereas knockdown of nuclear-enriched circ_753 preserved GJA1. Both induced lumen disruption, β-catenin disorganization, increased invasion, and regulated onco-miR-182. More pronounced miR-182 upregulation and broader repression of tumor-suppressive targets (BCL2, FOXO1, RECK) were observed in circ_753 knockdown cells, alongside concurrent depletion of hsa_circ_0008932 (circ_8932), which is predicted to interact with miR-182. Similar reciprocal changes in circRNA/miR-182 were observed in released EVs. These data highlight circRNA-miR-182 networks with distinct effects on tumor initiation and potential value as breast cancer biomarkers.

title: Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Reveals Molecular Differences Underlying Meiotic Competence of Brilliant Cresyl Blue (BCB) Selected Alpaca Oocytes.
abstract: Identifying oocytes with high meiotic competence remains a major challenge for improving in vitro embryo production in South American camelids. Although Brilliant Cresyl Blue (BCB) staining has been used to distinguish alpaca oocytes with different meiotic and developmental competence, the biological and molecular feature associated with their meiotic competence remain poorly understood. This study characterized the transcriptomic profiles of immature alpaca (Vicugna pacos) oocytes classified as BCB-positive (BCB+) or BCB-negative (BCB-) using single-cell RNA sequencing. BCB+ oocytes exhibited a significantly larger ooplasm diameter, a higher proportion of condensed chromatin configurations, and higher in vitro maturation rates than BCB- oocytes. Transcriptomic analysis identified 2978 differentially expressed genes and revealed a clear separation between groups (PC1 = 64.8%). Differentially expressed genes with higher transcript abundance in BCB+ oocytes were enriched in DNA metabolism, cell cycle, oocyte meiosis, and proteasome pathways, whereas those with higher transcript abundance in BCB- oocytes were enriched in gene expression regulation, RNA metabolism, chromatin remodeling, and intracellular signaling. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis identified distinct hub genes in each group, including CDK1, CCNB2, MAD2L1, and AURKB in BCB+ oocytes and EP300, CREBBP, SMARCA4, and ARID1A in BCB- oocytes. These results provide the first single-cell transcriptomic characterization of BCB-classified alpaca oocytes and establish the molecular basis underlying the biological differences identified by BCB staining.

title: Targeting Nupr1-Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b-Dependent Survival Program.
abstract: Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive. By integrating clinical observations and single-cell RNA sequencing, we found that Nuclear Protein 1 (Nupr1), a critical stress-responsive factor, is significantly upregulated in aortas from AD patients and murine models, with enrichment in VSMCs. Remarkably, VSMC-specific Nupr1 deficiency significantly ameliorated AD progression in vivo. Mechanistically, Nupr1 undergoes massive mitochondrial accumulation in Ang II-induced apoptotic VSMCs. Rather than operating as a conventional transcriptional regulator, mitochondrially enriched Nupr1 functions as a pathological spatial switch. It sequesters p53 within mitochondria, driving transcription-independent apoptosis while simultaneously blunting the protective Gadd45b-mediated survival program. Furthermore, in vivo Gadd45b overexpression was sufficient to rescue mitochondrial dysfunction and ameliorate vascular collapse. Taken together, our findings conceptualize the Nupr1-p53-Gadd45b axis as an important determinant of VSMC fate and provide a novel and promising therapeutic strategy for preventing AD progression.

title: Evolutionary logic and biotechnological potential of alternative splicing in higher eukaryotes: Comparative insights from plants and animals.
abstract: Alternative splicing (AS) generates transcript and protein isoforms, but its evolutionary significance cannot be inferred from isoform number alone. This review uses a comparative evidence framework to separate splice-variant origin, functional consequence, and evolutionary retention in plants and animals. We synthesize evidence from long-read sequencing, single-cell isoform profiling, pangenomics, proteogenomics, and perturbation studies. Animal studies emphasize exon-level switches in neural, cardiac, immune, and germline programs, whereas plant studies highlight intron retention, exitron splicing, environmental responses, and polyploidy-associated regulation. These are tendencies shaped by biological and sampling differences, not exclusive properties of either kingdom. Three worked examples illustrate how reproducible regulation, conservation or population evidence, molecular consequences, and targeted perturbation support different levels of inference. Functional effects alone do not establish historical adaptation, and conservation alone does not identify the trait under selection. The framework helps prioritize isoforms for crop improvement, biomarkers, and RNA intervention. Clinical splice modulation and field-evaluated natural rice alleles demonstrate translational potential, while highlighting the distinction between validated outcomes and prospective engineering. Future studies should connect isoform-resolved measurements to causal perturbation and fitness or agronomic performance across relevant environments.

title: Deciphering the Molecular and Cellular Landscape of Early Diabetic Nephropathy through Single-Cell RNA Sequencing and Protein-Protein Interaction Networks.
abstract: Diabetic nephropathy (DN) arises through complex pathological mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. This study employs transcriptomic and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) approaches to systematically characterize gene expression patterns, cellular composition changes, and intercellular communication networks in early DN. Analysis of the GSE111154 transcriptome dataset identified 259 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 118 protein-coding genes (70 downregulated and 189 upregulated) in DN samples. Functional enrichment analysis revealed significant involvement of these DEGs in immune response pathways and extracellular matrix (ECM) organization. Single-cell analysis of the GSE131882 dataset resolved 12 distinct renal cell populations, demonstrating significant shifts in cellular proportions in DN, with notable expansions of endothelial cells (ENDO), fibroblasts (FIB), principal cells (PC), and parietal epithelial cells (PEC). Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified COL1A2, FLNA, A2M, and PLG as central hub genes in DN pathogenesis. Cell-cell communication analysis revealed enhanced interaction frequency and intensity in DN, particularly involving FIB cells through specific signaling pathways including CDH5, KIT, THBS, EGF, and FN1. In DN originated FIBs, the differential genes enriched transcription factor was NR2F2. Through immunohistochemical staining, NR2F2 was up-expressed in DN samples while CD31 was down-regulated. These findings collectively demonstrate profound dysregulation of immune responses, ECM remodeling, and cellular crosstalk during DN progression, highlighting key molecular and cellular drivers of disease pathogenesis.

title: Cancer nanomedicine and RNA/Lipid nanoparticle platforms in oncology: developmental evolution, translational barriers, and precision-therapy opportunities.
abstract: Nanomedicine has become an important translational platform in oncology by enabling altered pharmacokinetics, controlled exposure, reduced systemic toxicity, intracellular delivery of nucleic acids, and improved handling of complex therapeutic payloads. Early cancer nanomedicines, including pegylated liposomal cytotoxics and albumin-bound drug products, demonstrated that nanoscale formulation design could improve the clinical utility of established anticancer agents. More recently, lipid nanoparticles, RNA therapeutics, individualized neoantigen vaccines, gene-regulatory approaches, and immune-modulating delivery systems have expanded the role of nanoparticles from passive drug carriers to programmable oncology platforms. This narrative review examines the developmental evolution of cancer-focused pharmaceutical nanoparticles, with emphasis on liposomes, lipid nanoparticles (LNPs), albumin-bound systems, polymeric particles, polymeric micelles, nanocrystals, nanoemulsions, solid lipid nanoparticles, inorganic particles, extracellular vesicles, and hybrid delivery technologies. Each platform class is treated systematically, covering representative approved products, formulation characteristics, route of administration, clinical evidence, and the specific development risks that limit it. There view connects platform design with oncology-specific barriers, including tumor heterogeneity, variable enhanced permeability and retention (EPR) effects, dense extracellular matrix, abnormal tumor vasculature, mononuclear phagocyte clearance, protein-corona formation, endosomal escape, immune activation, and the difficulty of translating animal tumor models into clinical benefit. These barriers are organized as a sequential delivery cascade, and the behavior of each platform class is compared step by step rather than described as a set of universal phenomena. Nanoparticle candidates that accumulated well in preclinical tumors but failed in clinical trials are examined alongside approved products, because the contrast between the two is where most of the transferable lessons sit. A product-development perspective is used to discuss critical quality attributes (CQAs), manufacturing scalability, potency testing, sterility strategy, stability, release methods, regulatory expectations, commercial feasibility, and clinical differentiation. A development-to-translation framework is proposed for comparing cancer nanomedicine platforms across formulation maturity, analytical maturity, manufacturing maturity, biological rationale, clinical evidence, regulatory readiness, and commercial feasibility; regulatory and commercial maturity are scored separately, the criteria behind each level are defined explicitly, and the resulting rankings are presented as a heuristic aid to discussion rather than a validated quantitative metric. Future progress in oncology nanomedicine will depend not only on novel materials or targeting claims, but also on disciplined product design, biologically meaningful potency assays, scalable manufacturing, patient-selection strategies, and clear integration with precision oncology.

title: The Maternal Blood Transcriptome Reflects Molecular Signatures Associated With Large Offspring Syndrome and Other Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Cattle.
abstract: Large offspring syndrome (LOS) in cattle is a phenomenon characterized by fetal overgrowth that is largely associated with calves derived from in vitro produced embryos. Here it was tested whether occurrence of LOS as well as two other adverse pregnancy outcomes, stillbirth and abortion, could be predicted using changes in the maternal blood transcriptome early in gestation. Blood samples were collected from Holstein and crossbred heifers at 40-50 days of gestation following embryo transfer of in vitro produced embryos. A total of 203 samples were selected for RNA-sequencing and used to compare recipients of embryos resulting in live-born calves of normal birth weight (control; n = 96) with recipients of embryos resulting in LOS calves (n = 15), stillbirths (n = 43), and abortion before 210 days of gestation (n = 49). Large offspring syndrome was defined based on birth weights greater than 2 standard deviations from the mean. The number of differentially-expressed genes (p < 0.01) was 32, 176, and 100 for comparisons of control versus LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively. Biomarkers were identified in a randomly selected, balanced training dataset using Random Forest after filtering for differential expression. Markers were then tested in the held-out dataset through 6 machine learning models. The best biomarkers consisted of 26, 24, and 28 genes for LOS, stillbirth and abortion, respectively. The accuracy of prediction ranged from 0.91 to 0.965 for LOS, 0.73 to 0.98 for stillbirth, and 0.62 to 0.96 for abortion. Despite the relatively small sample size, the model demonstrated high sensitivity for LOS classification, supporting that the maternal blood transcriptome in early pregnancy reflects molecular alterations associated with fetal overgrowth that can be predictive of the condition.

title: CD180-Associated B-Cell Alterations in Type 1 Diabetes and the In Vitro Effects of Chlorogenic Acid: An Integrated Transcriptomic and Experimental Study.
abstract: Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM) is an autoimmune disease involving progressive loss of pancreatic β-cells. Although B cells have been implicated in T1DM progression, the molecular characteristics associated with disease-related B-cell states remain unclear. Here, we investigated B-cell-associated molecular alterations in T1DM and explored the potential immunomodulatory effects of a natural compound. Public T1DM transcriptomic datasets were analyzed using differential expression analysis, WGCNA, and machine-learning approaches. Single-cell RNA sequencing was used to characterize Cd180 expression across B-cell states. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations were used to explore potential interactions between CD180 and candidate compounds, and an exploratory DARTS assay was performed to assess CGA-associated changes in CD180 proteolytic susceptibility. CD180 expression was examined in pancreatic tissues from vehicle- and MSA-2-treated NOD mice. The effects of chlorogenic acid (CGA) were evaluated in vitro by exposing B cells to CGA during inflammatory stimulation, followed by washing and co-culture with MIN6 cells in CGA-free medium. Integrated transcriptomic analysis identified four T1DM-associated genes (CD180, KCNJ2, STEAP4, and ZXDA), among which CD180 showed the strongest association with B-cell-related immune alterations. Single-cell analysis showed increased Cd180 expression in inflammatory B-cell states together with enrichment of antigen-presentation-related programs. An exploratory DARTS experiment with matched loading-control data suggested altered CD180 proteolytic susceptibility following CGA exposure, although independent reproducibility remains to be established. In vitro, CGA exposure during inflammatory stimulation was associated with reduced CD180 expression in B cells and improved MIN6 cell viability and insulin-secretory responses during subsequent co-culture in CGA-free medium. CD180 is associated with inflammatory B-cell alterations in T1DM and may represent a candidate molecular feature of B-cell dysregulation. CGA treatment was associated with changes in CD180 expression in activated B cells and improved β-cell functional outcomes in vitro. These findings support further investigation of the relationship between CGA and CD180; however, whether the effects of CGA are specifically mediated through CD180 requires further experimental validation.

title: Network pharmacology and single-cell sequencing analysis of gastrodin in anticancer effects against colorectal cancer by regulating key target genes and the tumor immune microenvironment.
abstract: Gastrodin is a natural compound with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antitumor activities; however, its therapeutic role and molecular mechanisms in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain unclear. In this study, we explored the anti-CRC mechanisms of gastrodin through integrated bioinformatics and experimental validation. The potential targets of gastrodin were obtained from public databases. Transcriptomic data of CRC were retrieved from TCGA and GEO datasets, and the differentially expressed genes were screened. The CRC-related genes were subjected to gene-set variation analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, and the core genes were identified by the LASSO regression, support vector machine, and random forest algorithms, followed by SHAP analysis. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), immune infiltration analysis, consensus clustering, molecular docking, and in vitro experiments were further performed. A total of 628 potential gastrodin targets and 15 overlapping CRC-related genes were identified. Five core hub genes, including NFE2L3, UBE2S, CA9, CCNB1, and CFD, were screened, among which NFE2L3 showed the highest SHAP importance score. The scRNA-seq data indicated cell-type-specific expression patterns of these genes in CRC tissues. Immune infiltration analysis further suggested that gastrodin may regulate the CRC immune microenvironment by regulating the activated B cells, activated CD4⁺ T cells, and other immune cells. Molecular docking revealed favorable binding affinity between gastrodin and the five core proteins. Moreover, NFE2L3 was highly expressed in CRC tissues and cell lines, and its knockdown significantly inhibited the proliferation, migration, and invasion of the tumor cells.
