Gastrodin may suppress CRC progression by targeting key genes, particularly NFE2L3, and modulating the tumor immune microenvironment. Furthermore, our study has identified the potential biomarkers and therapeutic targets for CRC.

title: Cytopathology and Prognostic Accuracy of 15-GEP/PRAME: The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group Study 2.
abstract: Gene expression profiling (GEP) reliably predicts metastatic uveal melanoma risk and is used to manage uveal melanoma (UM) in patients with this diagnosis. Efforts to refine molecular prognostication continue. To determine if confirmatory cytopathology findings influence the prognostic accuracy of a commercially available GEP/Preferentially Expressed Antigen in Melanoma (PRAME) assay. The Collaborative Ocular Oncology Group 2 study, a prospective cohort study, was conducted from 2017 to 2020 with follow-up recorded at 6-month intervals. This was a multicenter study that included patients with choroidal and/or ciliary body melanoma and results from a 15-GEP and PRAME RNA expression (15-GEP/PRAME) assay. Patients with iris tumors or less than 6 months' follow-up were excluded. Study data were analyzed from April 2025 to July 2026. 15-GEP/PRAME, cytopathology, and next-generation sequencing (NGS). Metastatic uveal melanoma rates in patients who had 15-GEP/PRAME and confirmatory cytopathology (CCP) results confirming or suspicious for UM (GEP+CCP) were compared with those who had 15-GEP/PRAME and no cytopathology performed, or unknown or nondiagnostic cytopathology results (GEP only). UM-associated variants identified by NGS were also evaluated. Of 1537 patients (mean [SD] age, 62.0 [13.4] years; 787 male [51.2%]), 727 (47.3%) had CCP results, and 810 (52.7%) had nondiagnostic cytopathology results or no cytopathology performed. Class 2/PRAME+ tumors were more common (136 of 727 [18.7%]) in the GEP+CCP group than in the GEP-only group (72 of 810 [8.9%]; 9.8% difference; 95% CI, 6.4-13.3; P <.001), whereas class 1/PRAME- tumors were less common (330 of 727 [45.4%] vs 495 of 810 [61.1%]; 15.7% difference; 95% CI, 10.8-20.6; P <.001). In patients with GEP+CCP, 22.7% (n = 165) developed metastasis vs 15.4% (n = 125) in patients with GEP only (7.3% difference, 95% CI, 3.3-11.2; P < .001). Adjusting for 15-GEP/PRAME status, there were no differences in metastasis rates between CCP groups. Of 1327 patients with successful NGS, 94.1% (605 of 643) in the GEP+CCP group and 71.9% (492 of 684) in the GEP-only group had a UM-associated variant (22.2% difference, 95% CI, 18.3-26.0; P < .001). Results of this cohort study reveal that no differences in metastasis outcomes were observed between patients with and without CCP within any GEP/PRAME categories. UM-associated variants were found less frequently in the GEP-only group than in the GEP+CCP group. In this cohort, 15-GEP/PRAME classification without CCP retained prognostic validity, supporting its clinical consideration in guiding metastatic surveillance in cases in which cytopathology is unavailable.

title: Combined Bioinformatic Analysis and RNA Sequencing Uncover Key Tinnitus-Related Molecules in the Cingulate Gyrus.
abstract: Tinnitus arises from maladaptive plasticity and abnormal synaptic function, not only in auditory pathways but also in limbic regions. Among these, the cingulate gyrus plays a pivotal part in shaping the emotional burden and sensory filtering disturbances often seen in tinnitus patients. Yet, the specific molecular players operating within this region remain poorly understood, and most existing bioinformatic predictions have not been tested in living systems. Here, we combined multi-database mining with in vivo transcriptomic profiling to identify and validate key proteins and pathways linked to tinnitus in the cingulate gyrus. We built and compared protein-protein interaction networks representing auditory perception, acoustic challenge, and tinnitus states, thereby pinning down candidate hub molecules. To verify these candidates, we used a noise-induced mouse model of tinnitus, confirmed the phenotype via gap prepulse inhibition of acoustic startle (GPIAS), and then performed RNA-seq and qPCR on cingulate gyrus tissue. The bioinformatic screens pointed to AKT1 and TNF as central hubs, suggestive of an inflammatory-survival signaling axis. In our animal experiments, RNA-seq showed a clear rise in Akt1 transcript levels in the tinnitus group, and functional enrichment analysis pointed to marked changes in extracellular matrix organization, cell adhesion, and cytokine receptor pathways. qPCR further corroborated the Akt1 upregulation. Taken together, our integrative strategy establishes AKT1 and TNF as topologically central hub proteins in the cingulate gyrus tinnitus network, and validates Akt1 upregulation in vivo, offering potential biomarker candidates and therapeutic leads for future studies.

title: The Novel Organic Arsenical PZ2 Exhibits Potent Anti-T-ALL Activity via ROS-Dependent Apoptosis and GABARAPL1-Induced Autophagic Cell Death.
abstract: Objective: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) is a highly aggressive hematological malignancy with poor overall prognosis. This study systematically evaluates the anti-leukemic therapeutic potential and underlying redox-driven mechanisms of PZ2, a novel organic arsenic compound, in T-ALL. Methods: The cytotoxicity of PZ2 against T-ALL cell lines and normal cells was assessed to determine its therapeutic window. RNA-seq was utilized to map transcriptomic alterations. Intracellular redox homeostasis, mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP), cell cycle, and apoptosis were evaluated using flow cytometry and fluorescence microscopy. Ultrastructural changes and key protein expressions were analyzed via TEM, RT-qPCR, and immunoblotting. In vivo efficacy was validated using a T-ALL cell-line-derived xenograft (CDX) mouse model. Results: PZ2 exhibited superior cytotoxicity and an improved safety profile compared to inorganic arsenic trioxide (ATO). Transcriptomic data indicated strong enrichment in apoptosis and autophagy-lysosome pathways. PZ2 induced profound mitochondrial oxidative stress, leading to ROS accumulation, MMP loss, and subsequent activation of caspase-dependent apoptosis-effects that were completely rescued by ROS scavengers. Furthermore, PZ2 triggered G2/M phase arrest and activated autophagic flux (upregulated GABARAPL1 and LC3-II, degraded p62). Notably, pharmacological inhibition of autophagy rescued PZ2-induced apoptosis, revealing a pro-death autophagic mechanism. In vivo, PZ2 significantly suppressed tumor growth and prolonged survival without overt systemic toxicity. Conclusions: PZ2 exhibits potent anti-T-ALL activity that may involve a dual mechanism: ROS-dependent mitochondrial apoptosis and pro-death autophagy potentially associated with GABARAPL1. This novel organic arsenical may represent a promising and potentially safer alternative for leukemia therapy, and these findings suggest a potential interplay between oxidative stress and autophagic cell death.

title: From Single-Cell Sequencing Data Analysis to Functional Validation: XCL1 is Associated with Glycolytic Metabolism in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a head and neck cancer with high morbidity and mortality. Glycolytic metabolism plays a crucial role in its progression, yet the molecular mechanisms regulating glycolysis in OSCC remain unclear. Single-cell RNA sequencing of the GSE247582 dataset was used to identify cell subsets, analyze metabolic pathway enrichment, and screen core candidate genes. TCGA data were used to validate gene expression. In vitro gain- and loss-of-function experiments, together with glycolysis inhibition, were performed to assess the effects of XCL1 on cell proliferation, apoptosis, and glycolysis-related metabolic parameters. Five cellular subgroups were identified, each with distinct metabolic characteristics. The glycolysis/gluconeogenesis pathway was markedly active in specific subsets. Fifteen candidate genes were identified through differential expression analysis, of which seven were significantly upregulated in OSCC tissues in both paired and unpaired TCGA analyses. XCL1 showed the most pronounced and consistent upregulation among the validated candidates and was selected for functional investigation. XCL1 knockdown significantly suppressed OSCC cell proliferation, induced apoptosis, and reduced glucose uptake, lactate production, ATP levels, LDH activity, and the expression of glycolytic enzymes, including HK2, PKM2, and LDHA. Conversely, XCL1 overexpression enhanced OSCC cell proliferation and glycolysis-related metabolic parameters and reduced apoptosis, whereas 2-DG attenuated these effects. XCL1 is associated with glycolysis-related metabolic alterations and OSCC cell growth in vitro. These findings support further investigation of XCL1 in OSCC, while in vivo studies and larger clinical cohorts are needed to further evaluate its biological and therapeutic relevance.

title: Identification of SGK1 as a candidate regulator associated with myeloid cell senescence in ME/CFS: An integrative transcriptomic and experimental study.
abstract: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS) is a complex illness lacking objective diagnostic biomarkers and clear pathophysiological understanding. Patients exhibit immune dysregulation and chronic inflammation reminiscent of aging phenotypes, yet the role of myeloid cell senescence in this disease remains unexplored. A stepwise integrative transcriptomic and computational strategy was employed. Differentially expressed genes were identified from the bulk transcriptomic dataset GSE14577. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis was performed to identify key modules correlated with the ME/CFS phenotype. Candidate genes were obtained by intersecting these modules with aging-related genes from the GenAge database. Core hub genes were further selected using LASSO regression and random forest machine learning algorithms. Cell type-specific expression was mapped using single-cell RNA sequencing data GSE214283, and functional validation was conducted via siRNA knockdown in a THP-1 cell senescence model. Integrative analysis identified HMGCR and SGK1 as core hub genes. Functional enrichment analysis revealed that candidate genes were enriched in pathways related to cellular senescence and inflammation. Single-cell transcriptomics analysis suggested that SGK1 expression was enriched in myeloid cell populations, including monocytes and neutrophils, in individuals with ME/CFS, whereas HMGCR showed a broader expression pattern. Single-gene GSEA indicated that SGK1 was associated with autophagy and lysosomal function. In vitro experiments showed that SGK1 expression was significantly upregulated in D-galactose-induced senescent THP-1 cells, and SGK1 knockdown markedly reduced the mRNA expression levels of senescence markers p16, p21, and p53. This study identifies SGK1 as a candidate molecule associated with myeloid cell senescence-related alterations in ME/CFS. Integrated transcriptomic, single-cell, and experimental analyses suggest a potential link between SGK1 expression and aging-associated immune alterations. However, further validation in primary ME/CFS-derived immune cells and clinical cohorts is required to determine the biological significance and clinical relevance of SGK1.

title: Pan-Fibrotic Gene Expression Signature in Major Chronic Diseases by Integrative Bulk and Single-Cell Transcriptomic Analyses.
abstract: Fibrosis is a shared feature of chronic liver, kidney and heart disease, yet no molecular signature captures the mechanisms common to these organs. We integrated human microarray, bulk and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) data across 2022 unique tissue samples to identify a conserved pan-fibrotic signature. The pan-fibrotic signature was defined in a microarray discovery cohort (n = 1051) and verified in a microarray liver (n = 325), two RNA-seq (n = 414) and four integrated snRNA-seq validation datasets (n = 69). Diagnostic models were built using five machine learning approaches in separate RNA-seq cohorts (training n = 209; liver validation n = 70; kidney validation n = 24). 492 fibrosis-associated genes were identified across organs, including 23 hallmark genes, a subset of which correlated with disease severity. A novel finding was consistent metallothionein (MT1E, MT1X) downregulation; snRNA-seq resolved cell-type-specific expression of 12 hallmark genes, including MT1E/MT1X predominantly expressed in hepatocytes and liver sinusoidal endothelial cells. Elastic Net performed best across all three gene sets (AUROC 0.765-0.830), with scores correlating significantly with interstitial fibrosis and tubular atrophy (%IFTA; rho 0.58-0.73). This study defines a cross-organ pan-fibrotic signature, providing potential candidate therapeutic targets and biomarkers applicable across tissues affected by fibrosis.

title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug sensitivity measurements into cell subtype- and single-cell-specific profiles. We first validate CLIMB using in-vitro mixtures of leukemic cell lines with experimentally known cell-type proportions, then extend this validation to large-scale, cross-dataset pseudo-bulk analyses built from independent scRNA-seq references across two disease contexts and five cancer types - mimicking the reference-to-target mismatches encountered in real applications - and show that CLIMB accurately infers the cellular composition of bulk samples, outperforming state-of-the-art bulk deconvolution methods. We emphasize CLIMB's effectiveness in acute myeloid leukemia, where it offers highly accurate estimation of leukemic stem cell fractions across three test datasets and three patient cohorts. We then validate CLIFF, our algorithm for estimating cell subtype- and single-cell-specific drug sensitivity, first on the same in-vitro cell line mixtures using experimentally measured drug responses, and then through in-depth, realistic-scale pseudo-bulk simulations. We applied our deconvolution strategy to the beatAML cohort dataset, currently the most extensive database of ex-vivo drug screening data. This analysis generated a cell subtype-resolved drug sensitivity landscape for 121 compounds, revealing multiple compounds putatively active against leukemic stem cells, including midostaurin, A-674563, SNS-032, and foretinib. Collectively, our work introduces a general computational framework for resolving bulk functional measurements at cell-type and single-cell resolution, providing an attractive new computational tool for drug development and precision medicine.

title: Inflammatory Network Remodeling in AML Is Driven by Neutrophil-Centric Self-Amplifying Circuits.
abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) progression involves remodeling of the bone marrow inflammatory microenvironment, yet prior studies have focused on individual cytokines rather than coordinated network-level communication. This study aimed to systematically map inflammatory network reprogramming in AML and develop a network-derived prognostic tool. Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on bone marrow samples from three newly diagnosed AML patients and six healthy donors (47,525 cells); ligand-receptor communication was then analyzed using CellChat. Communication dominance shifted from T-cells to myeloid populations, with networks restructured into neutrophil-centric computationally predicted self-amplifying circuits, exemplified by CXCL8-CXCR2 and CCL3-CCR1 axes. Despite the limited sample size of the scRNA-seq cohort (3 AML patients and 6 healthy donors), which may limit the generalizability of the detailed cellular and network findings, the subsequent protein-level Luminex validation in a larger cohort of 46 patients and 26 healthy controls provides robust support for the key findings. An inflammatory risk score (IRS) was constructed using LASSO-penalized Cox regression and evaluated for prognostic performance and integration with the European LeukemiaNet 2022 (ELN2022) classification. Luminex profiling confirmed dysregulation of key mediators, including reduced CCL3, CCL4, CXCL8, and IL-1A together with elevated CXCL10 in AML, and revealed substantial de-modularization of the cytokine correlation network. The IRS, based on CXCL8, CCL2, and IL-1A, achieved a concordance index of 0.729 for overall survival and stratified the ELN2022 intermediate-risk category into distinct prognostic subgroups. Inflammatory network pattern analysis provides a complementary dimension to genetic risk stratification in AML. The IRS captures microenvironment-derived prognostic information not reflected by current classification systems, though prospective multicenter validation is essential before clinical application.
